question: Measles has a basic reproduction number (R₀) of approximately 12–18, giving a herd immunity threshold of ~92–95%. A tribal village in Odisha achieves 60% measles vaccination coverage after a campaign. Which statement best describes the epidemiological consequence?

answers.text: Unvaccinated individuals remain at high risk because coverage is far below the herd immunity threshold needed to interrupt transmission

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. For measles (R₀ ≈ 12–18), approximately 92–95% of the population must be immune to break transmission chains. At 60% coverage, 40% of the population remains susceptible — far too large a pool for herd protection. The virus can still find enough non-immune hosts to sustain outbreaks, leaving unvaccinated individuals and those with waning immunity at substantial risk.

answers.text: The population is protected because more than half the people are immune

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. While 60% coverage protects those vaccinated individuals, it falls far short of the ~92–95% herd immunity threshold. With measles R₀ of 12–18, each case can infect 12–18 people in a fully susceptible population. The remaining 40% susceptible individuals provide a large enough pool for sustained transmission and outbreaks.

answers.text: The 60% who are vaccinated are now at equal risk as the unvaccinated because the vaccine fails at low coverage

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Vaccinated individuals retain their individual immune protection regardless of community coverage levels. However, the community lacks herd immunity because 60% is far below the ~92–95% threshold. This means unvaccinated individuals and those with incomplete responses remain at risk, as transmission chains are not interrupted.

answers.text: Herd immunity threshold is irrelevant for airborne pathogens like measles

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The herd immunity threshold applies to all communicable diseases, including airborne pathogens. In fact, airborne viruses like measles with high R₀ values require the highest thresholds. The formula H ≈ 1 − 1/R₀ applies regardless of transmission route — with R₀ of 12–18, measles requires ~92–95% population immunity to interrupt transmission.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember: herd immunity threshold ≈ 1 − 1/R₀. For measles (R₀ ≈ 12–18), approximately 92–95% of the population must be immune to interrupt transmission chains.
Well done! Understanding herd immunity thresholds is essential for public health vaccination strategy — measles requires among the highest coverage of any vaccine-preventable disease.
